text.p: The Polish Development Bank (PBR) has privately placed its first $50 million Eurobond at an issue price of 99.88, the bank said in a statement.
The three-year bonds, with a quarterly coupon, bear an interest of three month LIBOR plus 60 basis points.
They mature at the end of November 1999.
"We sold the issue without any problems," PBR's president Mieczyslaw Groszek told a news conference at which the statement was issued.
He added the bank was happy about the price at which the bonds were sold. "Financing at LIBOR plus 60 basis points is a small cost," he said.
The issue was led by Credit Suisse First Boston of the United States.
Shareholders of PBR have approved a issue of up to $75 million but Groszek said the bank sold only $50 million because it did not need more cash at the moment. @
"We could have sold much more...but considering our needs we settled for $50 million," he said.
Groszek said the bank would consider another Eurobond issue, possibly in other currencies.
"Next issues are likely to be easier, because we will already be known to investors. We would like to treat this issue more in terms of opening to the market than a one-off cash injection," he said.
PBR's issue will be the third Eurobond placement by a Polish bank after the country returned to international financial markets last year with an official $250 million issue.
Poland's rating by Moody's Investor Service is now Baa3, while that of Standard and Poor's is BBB minus and IBCA's BBB.
In the first half of 1996 PBR's net profits totalled 16 million zlotys, 66.6 percent more than in the same period of 1995, and most came from financial operations.
